exposure: Quality of sleep (measured by PSQI score)
outcome: Mode of birth (LSCS vs. Normal delivery)
cohort: Pregnant women in their first trimester who visited the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology O.P.D for antenatal visits, followed up to the post-partum period.
finding: Poor quality of sleep was significantly associated with poor fetal outcomes, including higher rates of mild/severe asphyxia, LSCS, preterm birth, low birth weight (<2.5 kg), and NICU admission.
mod_finding: PSQI score (indicating poorer sleep quality) was significantly higher in cases of LSCS compared to normal vaginal delivery.
birth_weight: Babies weighing <2.5 kg and >=2.5 kg were included; PSQI score was higher in the <2.5 kg group.
gest_age: Preterm and Term pregnancies were included; PSQI score was higher in preterm pregnancies, significant at the 3rd trimester.
